newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise on London Club debt news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise on London Club debt news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose further after news that significant progress had been made in reconciling Russia's commercial bank debt, and that a major portion had been reconciled, dealers said.
"Demand is high both from the West and Russian banks after the news. MinFins rose, tracking Vnesh debt," Sberbank dealer Sergei Abramov said.

Germany's Deutsche Bank AG said all outstanding issues regarding the documentation of Vnesheconombank's rescheduling was settled at a meeting on Wednesday of the Bank Advisory Committee on Vneshekonombank (VEB) debts, which is chaired by Deutsche.

Deutsche said VEB reported that it had acknowledged about 80 percent of banks' claims and that creditors had returned signed reconcilation statements of just under 20 percent of eligible debt, thereby approving the reconciliation.
Another dealer said the upward trend was stopped by brief profit-takings, but prices could edge up further when U.S. operators step in.
